newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end up on strong sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end up on strong sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended sharply up on Monday with investors snapping up blue chips and the Pudong real estate shares with sentiment boosted by the end of the annual reporting season, brokers said.
The B index surged 5.598 points or 6.14 percent to 96.817 points on volume of 56.566 million shares worth $31.604 million.
Both overseas and domestic investors were seen buying blue chips and the three Pudong real estate shares due to strong confidence in the market outlook, brokers said.
"The market is on a bull run with most investors believing that the index is still comparatively low considering A share performance," one broker said.
"The index has risen too fast recently, so it will have a correction after it tests the key psychological resistance level of 100 points," another broker said.
All 43 B shares traded, with 40 up, two flat and one down.
Market giant Shanghai Chlor Alkali was the star and traded the most actively on overseas institution buying, rising $0.034 or 10.00 percent limit-up to $0.374 on volume of 5.7 million shares.
Shanghai Worldbest followed on its good 1996 results, jumping $0.062 or 9.96 percent to $0.684 on volume of 1.7 million shares.

The Shanghai A share index ended sharply up despite negative news that the national share issue quota has been raised by a further five billion yuan. They said there was enough hot money on the market to absorb such a sum.
The index surged 56.800 points or 3.90 percent to 1,513.303 points on volume of 917.7 million shares worth 12.6 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index soared 200.515 points or 5.03 percent to 4,189.865 points.
Shanghai Shuanglu Electric Appliances was the star on talk of financial restructuring, surging 0.83 yuan or 10.04 percent to 9.09 yuan on volume of 1.6 million shares.
